experiment: C8 exploratory cross-family depth-two hierarchy with attention-aware Canaria grammar
interpretation: Level-2 joint adaptation improved over no Level-2 adaptation in all three exploratory seeds, so the relative hierarchy mechanism remained visible.
However, the attention-only candidate grammar did not preserve the four-block SmallViT teacher sufficiently: lower-IR NMSE averaged about 0.449 and replacement validation accuracy was poor.
Therefore C8 does not support a cross-family depth-two claim. The limiting factor is the candidate grammar, not evidence of uncontrolled extra hierarchy cost.
A richer exact-matched grammar containing both token mixing and feed-forward nonlinearity should be explored before any fresh confirmatory cross-family depth-two test.
